title: Slow magnetic relaxation in a novel heptanuclear Dy cluster with five edge-sharing Dy3 triangles

material_class.structural_family: heptanuclear Dy7 cluster with five edge-sharing Dy3 triangles, {Dy7(μ3-OH)5} core

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, o-vanillin (0.061 g, 0.4 mmol), hydroxylamine chloride (0.028 g, 0.4 mmol), sodium benzoate (0.058 g, 0.4 mmol) and triethylamine (0.04 g, 0.8 mmol) were dissolved in methanol (30 mL) and stirred for 1 h (in situ oxime ligand formation). DyCl3·6H2O (0.148 g, 0.4 mmol) was then added, turning the solution light yellow. After stirring for 3 h the solution was filtered and the filtrate was left undisturbed to give light yellow crystals of 1 (yield 70%).
synthesis.time: stir 1 h before Dy addition, then 3 h after Dy addition, followed by undisturbed crystallization
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic solution reaction; filtration then undisturbed crystallization of the filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solution filtered; filtrate left undisturbed to give light yellow crystals of 1

properties.summary: DC susceptibility of polycrystalline 1 (300–2 K, 0.5 kOe) shows χMT = 98.75 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature (expected 99.19 for seven uncoupled Dy3+), decreasing to 75.83 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, attributed to weak Dy···Dy interactions and Stark-level depopulation. Magnetization at 2 K reaches 39.88 μB at 7 T without saturation, consistent with anisotropy and/or low-lying excited states. Zero-dc-field AC data (1.8–8 K, 5 G, 1–997 Hz) show frequency-dependent in-phase and out-of-phase signals indicating onset of slow magnetization relaxation and possible SMM behavior, but χ″ maxima were not observed down to 1.8 K so an Arrhenius barrier could not be extracted.
